correctness.rationale: The unique ridge simplex optimum satisfies (G^T v+rho lambda)·(e_i-lambda)>=0 for every vertex. Maximizing lambda_i-||lambda||^2 over the simplex gives exactly (m-1)/(4m), including all boundary cases. Explicit all-m two-vector-family KKT equations attain equality and maintain non-Pareto-stationarity. Exact strongly convex quadratics have component increase 3/8 at the stated full step while a common descent direction exists. verify.py reproduces rational finite checks independently of the algebraic proof; no incomplete enumeration is used for infinite quantifiers.

originality.rationale: Exact operator comparison: the 2026 source states a componentwise projected-step bound with half the useful negative quadratic coefficient and twice the sharp ridge penalty; its unconstrained specialization certifies negative derivative only for norm-square greater than rho(m-1)/m. Here the threshold is rho(m-1)/(4m), with equality for each objective count and a strict ascent witness. Closely related 2022 simplex-ridge method is already acknowledged, including its parameter scaling; its inspected gradient-tracking and convergence analysis does not provide the exact finite-step margin. Residual risk is equivalent unindexed optimization inequalities derived from elementary KKT geometry.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent constant may occur in unindexed literature under a regularized monotone-map variational inequality or a differently normalized simplex projection.
The sharp guarantee concerns the unconstrained exact multiplier; it must not be read as improving Li et al.’s general constrained lemma.
Only material recorded from relevant full-text regions was compared, not a line-by-line evaluation of every independent preprint cited by these articles.

value.rationale: Addresses a concrete gap in finite-step componentwise descent assessment for the exact multiplier used by a recent function-free projected-gradient method: the universal, computable sufficient condition in the unconstrained regime admits fourfold more ridge relative to squared gradient norm than the source Lemma 4.1 specialization. An all-m sharp obstruction and coercive strongly convex ascent example establish that the constant is structurally necessary; this is not an arbitrary parameter substitution or a general algorithm-failure claim.
